page: Microsoft Azure E32d_v5 is an EDv5 family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration includes 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores with hyper-threading) and a substantial 256.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1229 GB SSD, while no GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks place the E32d_v5 mostly in the average tier. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1633.0 and a multi-core score of 13826.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 36908.39. Memory bandwidth tests show 1679.85 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 148.27 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Notably, the server demonstrates strong text generation performance for small LLM models (135M) at 280.92 tokens/sec, though performance drops significantly for larger models, registering a weak 6.65 tokens/sec for 70B model prompt processing.

From a resource density perspective, the E32d_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio (1:8) and bundled local SSD storage, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. However, the tradeoff lies in its average compute performance across standard benchmarks, meaning it is less optimized for pure compute-bound tasks compared to specialized compute instances.

This server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale web serving. Its high memory capacity and local SSD storage make it appropriate for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and data processing tasks.
